title: TSMC Q3 Earnings Preview Faces High Bar Amid AI Stock Jitters
summary: Gotrade News - Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) reported third-quarter 2026 net income of NT$763.06 billion on Thursday, October 15, up 68.7% year
body_markdown:
Gross margin landed inside the guided range but slightly under the 66.5% Hudson Labs consensus and the 67.5% Morgan Stanley had forecast, according to[Admirals](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview) . Management had warned that the 2-nanometer ramp would dilute second-half gross margin by 3 to 4 percentage points, per[TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/tsmcs-q3-earnings-preview-65-profit-growth-but-net-margin-seen-slipping-to-50) . The release shows 2nm already accounted for 8% of wafer revenue in the quarter, with 3nm at 33% and 5nm at 28%.


## TSMC Guides Q4 Revenue to US$52.3 Billion to US$54.3 Billion


For the fourth quarter, TSMC expects revenue of US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion, gross margin of 65% to 67% and operating margin of 56.5% to 58.5%, based on an exchange rate of 31.8 NT dollars per US dollar, according to the[company's release](https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3346) . Ahead of the report, Morgan Stanley had forecast fourth-quarter revenue growth of 10% to 15% from the third quarter, as reported by[Admirals](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview) .


> "Moving into fourth quarter 2026, we expect our business to be supported by continued strong demand," said TSMC CFO Wendell Huang, pointing to the steep ramp of the company's 2-nanometer technology.


Huang also said third-quarter business was supported by strong demand for TSMC's leading-edge process technologies, per the[release](https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3346) .


## Why AI Stock Jitters Raised the Bar for TSM


The print arrived after a shaky stretch for AI-linked stocks. On October 8, chipmakers fell 3.4%,[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) dropped 2.9% and[Intel (INTC)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/intc/) slid 5.3% after OpenAI said its annualized revenue was close to US$50 billion at the end of September, about US$20 billion below earlier figures, according to[Admirals](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview) . TSM's ADR lost 3.01% that day to US$457.99, in the Nasdaq's worst session since mid-August.


Per[Admirals](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview) , TSM's ADR closed at US$453.31 on October 9, 6.7% below its record close of US$485.80 on October 5. Options had priced in a move of about 4.3% in either direction around the results, and the stock fell 3.8% after its July report.


Macro pressure added to the caution. The US 10-year Treasury yield sat near 5.23% on October 8, a 24-year high, and investors were also weighing the[September US CPI report due October 14](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/cpi-tonight-as-bofa-and-morgan-stanley-report/) , according to[Admirals](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview) .


## What Analysts Watch After TSMC's Beat


Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan expected TSMC to lift its full-year revenue growth guidance to the low-to-mid 40% range from above 40%, as reported by[TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/tsmcs-q3-earnings-preview-65-profit-growth-but-net-margin-seen-slipping-to-50) . TSMC raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to US$60 billion to US$64 billion in July, per[Admirals](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview) , a sign of how much leading-edge capacity the company is building for AI demand.


Consensus estimates keep TSMC's net margin at about 50% to 51% each quarter through the third quarter of 2027, according to[TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/tsmcs-q3-earnings-preview-65-profit-growth-but-net-margin-seen-slipping-to-50) , so the 2nm margin drag and any update to full-year growth targets on the earnings call are likely to shape how investors read the quarter.
